notes: Drafted by tools/claw/draft_spec.py from the disassembly. Indirect receivers (settled 2026-10-20, level-one-indirect-receiver-repair): in 0x46c2c0 every self call has ECX = self (the entry receiver, held in EBP): slot +0x50 at 0x46c4cc, +0x10 at 0x46c514 and +0x64 at 0x46c593. Slot +0x50 takes two stack arguments (the word at [self+0x14c], then the count) that the callee does not pop: the caller reuses them as the last two formatter arguments and removes them with its add esp after 0x4a3920. It is therefore not a callee-pop thiscall and cannot be a harness stub (a cdecl stub refuses a receiver, a thiscall stub pops); cases supply it with an original function that reads ECX and returns with a plain RET, for example 0x40af20 (returns [ECX+0x34]), so that a receiver of 0 faults or differs. Native code must call it as run.call(slot, self, {layer, count}). The surface slots +0x44 (0x46c561) and +0x68 (0x46c60d) are COM methods with the interface pointer as first stack argument; their ECX is incidental. The other indirect sites in this family already pass the original receivers (0x462350 via vcall, 0x462af0 handler entries with the entry receiver, 0x4631e0 +0x44 via vcall, 0x46a8d0 +0x24/+0x34 via vcall, 0x462410 calls through a register holding an import).
